decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display fits the firm's core cardboard display range, and with only one year on the market and no reported shortfall against aspirations, a large firm's slack lets it keep the product while results are still uncertain.
The pegboard-back shelf display extends the established display line at low marginal cost, so there is no clear performance gap to trigger problemistic search this early.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a staple format for retail promotions and likely meets aspirations based on the firm's past display business.
The eighth-pallet display complements the quarter-pallet range for smaller retail spaces, and the firm has enough slack to carry it while it builds sales.
The wooden display pallet lies outside the firm's core paper competence and is more likely to fall short of aspirations, but one year is too early to drop it given the firm's slack.
The media-product display serves a shrinking physical media market, which raises the risk of a shortfall, but there is not yet enough evidence to withdraw it.
